pool.text: Local shepherd Appak Baizhanov allegedly found coal prompting a coal mining boom in Karaganda.
Coal mining in the area resumed and temporary structures were built for miners.
Coal production in Karaganda was below expectations during this year.
Karaganda was incorporated as a village before later being declared a city.
The area was connected via railroad bringing supplies and highly-qualified personnel.
Karaganda was officially declared a city following its earlier village incorporation.
Master plans for Karaganda were laid out led by planner Alexander Ivanovich Kuznetsov.
Karaganda had a population of about 100,000 with about half being prisoners.
Karaganda suffered severe electromagnetic pulse effects when its electrical power plant caught fire.
The Karaganda Circus was constructed and criticized for its high cost.
An art installation was installed in Karaganda dedicated to a popular phrase.
A monument to a popular catchphrase was established in Karaganda.
The Catholic Cathedral of the Blessed Virgin Mary of Fatima was opened.
Archaeologists unearthed remains of a young couple buried face to face.
A new monument to the victims of the Holodomor was opened at the Karaganda Ethnopark.
The Kostenko coal mine caught fire, killing at least 32 people.
